For any amount, once the contract holds funds, an owner call to withdraw() must empty the contract's entire balance (address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant deletes the transfer so the balance stays unchanged.
For any amount the contract holds, a withdrawal by the owner must transfer the entire balance out so that address(c).balance becomes 0; the mutant deletes the transfer so the balance remains nonzero.

For any amount of Ether the contract holds, a withdraw() call by the Owner must succeed and transfer out the full balance so address(c).balance becomes 0; the mutant deletes the transfer so the balance remains unchanged (nonzero) after a successful owner withdraw.

For any positive balance the contract holds, a withdraw() call by the Owner must succeed and transfer out the entire balance so address(c).balance becomes 0; the mutant deletes the transfer so the balance stays positive (and behavior diverges) after every owner withdrawal.

For any positive balance, a withdraw() call by an Owner that cannot receive Ether must revert (because P's transfer to Owner fails and reverts); the mutant M deletes the transfer, so such a withdraw succeeds, violating the rule.

For any caller and any forwarded amount, Command must send exactly msg.value to the target, leaving the contract's overall Ether balance unchanged; the mutant instead forwards the entire balance, draining previously held funds and violating the invariant that address(c).balance after Command equals the balance before minus msg.value.

For any caller, value and non-empty calldata, Command to a contract that accepts ether only through a payable fallback (its receive reverts) must succeed; the mutant replaces the low-level call with a bare transfer that hits the reverting receive, so Command reverts for those inputs.

For any owner call to Command carrying arbitrary calldata, C executes it via an unchecked low-level call (Command always succeeds and, when the calldata makes a helper selfdestruct its balance to C, C's balance grows by that amount); the mutant ignores the calldata and instead bare-transfers, which reverts against a contract without a payable fallback and leaves C's balance unchanged.

For every call to multiplicate with msg.value below the contract's balance, C leaves the contract's ETH balance unchanged (the guarded branch is skipped), whereas the mutant drains the entire balance on any call, so the balance is no longer preserved.
